title: A finitely generated field is the fraction field of a quotient of a polynomial ring by a regular sequence, with n - c = trdeg
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is finitely generated: $K=k(b_1,\dots,b_m)$ for finitely many $b_1,\dots,b_m\in K$. Let $x_1,\dots,x_d\in K$ ($d\ge0$) be a finite transcendence basis of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Then there are integers $n\ge c\ge0$ with $n-c=d$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in k[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which form a regular sequence in the ring $k[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $\iota:A\to K$, where $A=k[X_1,\dots,X_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, such that (a) $\iota$ is injective, and (b) every element of $K$ equals $\iota(a)\,\iota(s)^{-1}$ for some $a,s\in A$ with $s\neq0$. In particular $A$ is an integral domain, and $\iota$ induces an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $S^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, $a/s\mapsto\iota(a)\iota(s)^{-1}$, where $S=A\setminus\{0\}$ and $S^{-1}A$ is the ring of fractions of $A$ with respect to $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangular-field-model-weak-regularity] for weak regularity. The unital map A -> K forces 1 != 0 in A. If the defining ideal were top, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem would give 1=0 and its image would contradict 1!=0 in K. Thus the ideal is proper, which, together with weak regularity, gives regularity. Use Ideal.smul_eq_mul and Ideal.mul_top to match top_ne_smul.

proof.text: Function.Injective.isDomain pulls back the domain structure from K. IsFractionRing.liftAlgHom lifts the injection to an algebra homomorphism FractionRing A -> K. It is injective as a homomorphism from a field. Given z=iota(a)/iota(s), turn s!=0 into membership in nonZeroDivisors A and use Localization.mk a s as a preimage; IsFractionRing.lift_mk' proves its image is z. AlgEquiv.ofBijective gives the asserted equivalence, with the formula on LocalizedModule.mk (definitionally Localization.mk).
